questions.question: Do you sell drones as well as accessories?
questions.answer: Yes. New and used DJI drones are listed in the Drones category of the shop. Stock changes often, so message us if you are looking for a specific model.

questions.question: Are your used drones tested?
questions.answer: Yes. Every used drone is checked before it is sold, and you can test it with us before you pay. Battery cycle counts are listed on the product when we have them.

questions.question: Do drones come with a warranty?
questions.answer: Our used drones come with a short shop warranty, and new sealed drones come with the standard DJI warranty. We confirm the warranty for your drone on WhatsApp.

questions.question: Which drone is best for beginners?
questions.answer: For most beginners we recommend a DJI Mini or DJI Neo. They are light, easy to fly, and have GPS hold and return-to-home. The Mini 3 Pro, Mini 4 Pro and Mini 5 Pro add obstacle sensing, which helps avoid crashes. Our blog has a full guide to every DJI model.

questions.question: What is a Fly More Combo?
questions.answer: It is DJI's bundle that adds extra batteries, a charging hub, spare propellers and a carry bag to the drone. It is usually the best value if you plan to fly often, because one battery only gives around 20 to 35 minutes of flight.

questions.question: What does "under 250 g" mean?
questions.answer: Drones that weigh less than 250 grams, such as the DJI Mini and Neo series, are the lightest category. In many countries they face fewer rules. Heavier batteries, such as Plus batteries, can push a drone over 250 g.

questions.question: Do you buy or trade in used drones?
questions.answer: Message us on WhatsApp with your drone model, its condition and photos, and we will let you know if we can buy it or take it in trade.

questions.question: How much does a good beginner drone cost?
questions.answer: A small camera drone like the DJI Neo or an older DJI Mini starts at a few hundred dollars. Newer Mini models with better cameras and obstacle sensing cost more. Used drones in good condition are a great way to start for less.

questions.question: What do I need to get started?
questions.answer: The drone, its remote, at least one battery, a charger, a microSD card and the DJI Fly app on your phone. Extra batteries, spare propellers and a case make flying much easier.

questions.question: Can a drone follow me by itself?
questions.answer: Many DJI drones can, using a feature called ActiveTrack or Follow Me. It is available on models like the Mini 3 Pro, Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro, Neo and Air series, but not on the basic Mini 2 or Mini 3.

questions.question: Will the drone avoid hitting things?
questions.answer: Only drones with obstacle sensors can, such as the Mini 4 Pro, Mini 5 Pro and Air series. Cheaper models have no sensors, and even drones with sensors can miss thin branches and wires, so always fly carefully.

questions.question: How good is the camera?
questions.answer: Most DJI drones shoot 4K video and sharp photos, and the newer Mini, Air and Mavic models handle low light much better. For social media, models with vertical shooting are very handy.

questions.question: What is the difference between a camera drone and an FPV drone?
questions.answer: A camera drone like the Mini flies smoothly and is made for photos and video. An FPV drone like the Avata or Neo with goggles lets you see from the drone in real time, for an immersive, fast flying experience.

questions.question: Can I buy DJI Care for a used drone?
questions.answer: DJI Care Refresh can usually only be bought within a short time after the drone is first activated, so most used drones cannot get it. Ask us on WhatsApp and we will check for your drone.

questions.question: What should I do before my first flight?
questions.answer: Update the drone, remote and batteries in the DJI Fly app, calibrate the compass if asked, and fly in an open area with a good GPS signal. Set a safe return-to-home height and start in Normal mode, not Sport.

questions.question: What do propeller guards do?
questions.answer: Propeller guards protect the propellers and the people around them, which is very useful indoors or while learning. They add a little weight, so expect slightly shorter flights and more drift in wind.

questions.question: How far can a drone fly?
questions.answer: It depends on the model. Small drones like the DJI Neo fly a few hundred metres with a phone, while DJI Mini, Air and Mavic drones can reach 10 to 20 km in open areas with no interference. In cities and near buildings the real range is much shorter, usually 1 to 4 km. Always keep your drone where you can see it.

questions.question: How high can a drone fly?
questions.answer: DJI drones can be set to fly up to 500 m above the take-off point in the DJI Fly app. For safety, most pilots stay below 120 m, which is the limit used in most countries.

questions.question: How long does a battery last in the air?
questions.answer: Most DJI drones fly 20 to 45 minutes per battery, depending on the model. Wind, cold weather and fast flying shorten it. Plan to land with around 20 to 30 percent battery left.

questions.question: What happens if the drone loses signal?
questions.answer: DJI drones have Return to Home. If the signal is lost or the battery gets low, the drone flies back and lands where it took off. Set a return height above nearby trees and buildings before you fly.

questions.question: Can I fly in wind or rain?
questions.answer: Light wind is fine, but small drones drift and drain the battery faster in strong wind. Avoid flying in rain or fog, because most drones are not waterproof.

questions.question: Can I fly at night?
questions.answer: Yes, the drone can fly at night, but obstacle sensing works poorly in the dark and it is harder to keep the drone in sight. Fly only in open areas you already know.

questions.question: Do I need my phone or internet to fly?
questions.answer: Drones with a screen remote like the DJI RC or RC 2 do not need a phone. With the standard remote, you connect your phone and use the DJI Fly app. Internet is only needed for maps, updates and activating a new drone.

questions.question: How fast can a drone fly?
questions.answer: Most DJI Mini drones reach about 55 km/h in Sport mode, and bigger models are faster. Use Normal mode while learning, because Sport mode turns off obstacle sensing.

questions.question: Do I need a memory card?
questions.answer: Most DJI drones need a microSD card to save photos and videos. Use a fast card (V30 or U3) of at least 64 GB.

questions.question: Is it hard to learn to fly?
questions.answer: No. DJI drones hover in place by themselves with GPS, so the basics take minutes. Practise take-off, landing and simple turns in an open field before trying longer flights.

questions.question: What if I crash my drone?
questions.answer: Bring it to us. Broken propellers, arms and many other parts can be replaced, and we will tell you on WhatsApp what can be fixed.

questions.question: Can I fly over the sea?
questions.answer: Yes, but take extra care. Over water the drone can drift, the downward sensors can get confused, and a drone that falls into salt water is usually lost. Keep good battery left and stay close.

questions.question: Is a drone loud?
questions.answer: Small drones like the Mini sound like a loud buzz up close, but are hard to hear once they are high in the air. Bigger drones are louder.

questions.question: Can a child fly a drone?
questions.answer: Older children can learn with an adult nearby. Start with a small, light drone in Normal mode and propeller guards, in an open area away from people.

questions.question: How many cycles is a good drone battery?
questions.answer: DJI batteries stay healthy for a few hundred charge cycles if they are looked after. A battery with fewer than 50 cycles is still in very good condition. Check the battery health in the DJI Fly app.

questions.question: How should I store drone batteries?
questions.answer: Store batteries at about 50 to 60 percent charge, in a cool and dry place. Avoid leaving them fully charged or empty for weeks, and never charge a battery that is swollen or damaged.

questions.question: How often should I change propellers?
questions.answer: Replace a propeller as soon as it is chipped, cracked or bent, even slightly. Damaged propellers cause vibration and can fail in flight. Spare propellers are cheap, so keep a set in your bag.

questions.question: How long does it take to charge a battery?
questions.answer: Most DJI batteries charge in about 1 to 1.5 hours. A charging hub charges several batteries one after another, so you can leave them all plugged in.

questions.question: Do I need to update the drone?
questions.answer: Yes. Update the drone, remote and batteries in the DJI Fly app when asked. Updates fix bugs and improve flying, so do them at home before a flight, not in the field.
